note: 56 Fact sentences in bigger_picture.json (60 cited entries, all present in report_ids.json) plus 5 attributed fact sentences in bigger_picture_bulletin.json. No tickers, no buy or sell advice, no citations or item ids in the Bulletin. Markets share recomputed: 772 of 4052 words, 19.1 percent.

problems.where: S1 '1. What AI can do now', paragraph 0, Fact {C01-01}
problems.quote: the price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens
problems.problem: The entry calls it a launch price and facts/C01-01 say it is introductory, rising to $4 and $20 later. Leaving that out makes the price sound permanent.
problems.suggested_fix: the launch price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens

problems.quote: the first judgement of these models will come from closed groups whose findings the rest of us cannot check
problems.problem: This fits Google's closed Fairwind group but not Anthropic. OSS Scanner is an opt-in service for public open-source projects, and C03-01 does not say its findings are closed or uncheckable.
problems.suggested_fix: Inference: the strongest models are being pointed first at security; Google's first judgement will come from a closed group of defenders whose findings the public cannot check.

problems.quote: the labs have begun to charge for time, not only for capability
problems.problem: The premium speed tier rests on one TokenPost report that cites no OpenAI statement (C01-02). The inference states it flatly, without that hedge.
problems.suggested_fix: if the reported Ultrafast tier is confirmed, the labs have begun to charge for time, not only for capability

problems.where: S2 '2. People and society', paragraph 1, Inference
problems.quote: the first licensed music deal shows one route by which creators get paid
problems.problem: Invented 'first'. facts/C06-08 say ElevenLabs already has music licensing deals with Merlin and Kobalt.
problems.suggested_fix: the UMG deal shows one route by which creators get paid

problems.quote: the only bill on the table concerns the Pentagon's suppliers
problems.problem: Stronger than the sources. C13-04 is one bill among today's stories, and nothing cited says there is no other AI bill.
problems.suggested_fix: the one bill in today's news concerns the Pentagon's suppliers

problems.where: S3 '3. Safety, security and law', paragraph 1, Inference
problems.quote: from Seoul's self-assessment order to the card industry's human-approval line, is the same one: an AI agent may look, but a person must say yes
problems.problem: Does not follow from C12-08. South Korea's 12-point security self-assessment says nothing about human approval of AI agents, so only the PCI guidance (C12-06) supports the rule.
problems.suggested_fix: Inference: the card industry's first rule for AI agents is that an agent may look but a person must say yes; Seoul's response so far is a security self-assessment, not an AI rule.

problems.quote: China Daily reports that seven central government departments published draft rules ... that would give gig workers employment contracts and require a person to review any algorithm's decision
problems.problem: Misattribution. The entry says China Daily reports the draft, and that Free Malaysia Today adds the contracts and human-review duty.
problems.suggested_fix: China Daily reports that seven central government departments published draft rules for gig workers, open for comment until 8 November; Free Malaysia Today adds that they would require employment contracts and a person to review any algorithm's decision to stop a worker's orders or ban an account; the final text may differ

problems.quote: in the United States it moves by lawsuit and letter, while Australia and China draft the first duties for AI that acts rather than answers ... Scenario: the USA Today suit matters more for what it adds to the queue
problems.problem: No cited US 'letter' exists (the ICO is British), and 'the first duties' is unsupported. The 'Scenario' sentence has no probability and is really an inference, so the label is wrong.
problems.suggested_fix: in the United States it moves by lawsuit, while Australia and China draft duties for AI that acts rather than answers ... Inference: the USA Today suit matters more for what it adds to the queue ...

problems.quote: much of the money goes to independent testing of whether the machines work, the step the AI build skipped
problems.problem: 'The step the AI build skipped' is an unsupported claim that no cited entry backs.
problems.suggested_fix: much of the money goes to independent testing of whether the machines can really be built large

problems.quote: yet the correction alone moved a major OpenAI investor's shares by 5%
problems.problem: Contradicts the hedge in C07-05, which says bond-market stress and higher oil prices also weighed. 'Alone' makes the claim stronger than the source.
problems.suggested_fix: yet the correction was followed by a 5% fall in a major OpenAI investor's shares, with bond stress and oil also weighing

problems.quote: whichever definition wins will make one of them look $20 billion smaller on the day
problems.problem: Invented figure. The $20 billion gap is OpenAI's own under the two methods (C06-04). Nothing cited gives Anthropic's gap, which is also not 'one of them' in the sense used.
problems.suggested_fix: whichever definition wins will make one of them look smaller on the day; for OpenAI the difference was about $20 billion

problems.quote: Markets share of this analysis: 19 percent of sections 1 to 5 by word count, within the quarter allowed by the Full Report rules (3 Oct 2026: 15 percent).
problems.problem: A process note printed in the reader-facing analysis, outside any labelled data-gap section. The figure itself is right (19.1 percent).
problems.suggested_fix: Remove the line from the published text and keep the figure in the QA log.

problems.quote: three scenarios that exclude each other and add up to 100 percent ... (c) ... OpenAI closes at or above $1.4 trillion ... Probability 15 percent
problems.problem: The probabilities sum to 100, but the scenarios are not clearly exhaustive: a quiet quarter with no freeze, no OpenAI close and rounds on target fits none of them. Scenario (c) also clashes with forecast 1, which puts an OpenAI round at about $1.4 trillion at 50 percent while (c), the only scenario with that outcome, gets 15 percent.
problems.suggested_fix: Define (a) as the base case, 'rounds keep closing on or below target, no freeze', so the three cover every outcome. Then either bring forecast 1 into line with (c), or state in (a) that OpenAI closing near $1.4 trillion with dearer debt elsewhere falls under (a).

problems.quote: by the end of January. Probability 65 percent. Horizon: 1 to 3 months.
problems.problem: Horizon mismatch. From 9 October, the end of January is almost 4 months away, outside the 1 to 3 months band.
problems.suggested_fix: by early January (Horizon: 1 to 3 months), or keep the end of January and set Horizon: 3 to 12 months

problems.quote: Chinese chipmakers are reported to have raised prices 20% to 50% on grey-market memory costs
problems.problem: C08-10's sources blame a worldwide HBM shortage; the grey market is how Chinese firms buy, not the stated cause. Also 20% to 50% is Huawei's range, while Cambricon's is 20% to 30%.
problems.suggested_fix: Chinese chipmakers are reported to have raised prices by 20% to 50%, citing a worldwide memory shortage

problems.quote: it is the first organised refusal by a scientific field to work with a lab
problems.problem: Stronger than the source and partly invented. C04-01 says the boycott is one group's position, not a field-wide decision, and nothing supports 'first'.
problems.suggested_fix: it is an organised call by a group of leading mathematicians to stop working with a lab

problems.quote: the fund manager quoted by Reuters says the former
problems.problem: Overstates the quote. Per C06-01, she called it 'an important reality check' but not the end of the AI trade; she did not blame Firmus's own debt and record.
problems.suggested_fix: the fund manager quoted by Reuters calls it a reality check, not the end of the AI boom

problems.where: D. Key unknowns, last Missing data
problems.quote: each entry names the relay it used {C06-04} {C06-01} {C09-03} {C07-07}
problems.problem: Not true. The summaries of C06-04, C06-01 and C07-07 name no relay; only C09-03 does (The Next Web).
problems.suggested_fix: drop 'each entry names the relay it used', or say 'the relays are recorded in our source notes'

problems.quote: A $20 billion counting change moved a major backer's shares by 5%
problems.problem: Contradicts the Bulletin's own paragraph 1 and C07-05, which say bond-market stress and oil also weighed.
problems.suggested_fix: A $20 billion counting change was followed by a 5% fall in a major backer's shares

problems.quote: a builder with debt and no record could not sell shares at all
problems.problem: Stronger than C06-01 and the Full Report, which say a short record, and an IPO shelved after lukewarm demand. Firmus now seeks private money.
problems.suggested_fix: a builder with heavy debt and a short record shelved its share sale

problems.quote: Memory, optical links and power are getting dearer too
problems.problem: Only memory-linked chip prices are reported as rising (C08-10). For optical links Lumentum reports a shortage, not a price rise (C08-08). Oracle's trucked gas is one firm's workaround, not power getting dearer generally.
problems.suggested_fix: Memory is getting dearer and optical parts are sold out, so building costs more as borrowing does.

problems.quote: with Chinese chip prices up 20% to 50% and Lumentum sold out to 2029
problems.problem: Drops the hedges. The price rises come from three unnamed people (Huawei 20% to 50%, Cambricon 20% to 30%), and 'sold out to 2029' is Lumentum's chief executive's own claim. The Full Report keeps both hedges.
problems.suggested_fix: with Chinese chip prices reported up 20% to 50% and Lumentum's chief executive saying it is sold out to 2029
